title: Research: fixed-z0 eight-transfer optimum and two-root boundary
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds the self-contained `research/scalable-dirty-connectors/` package with two optimality results for the universal arbitrary-dirty F2 connector:

- **Fixed-z0 endpoint:** for five sources with every source/output call at z0, eight bidirectional transfers are necessary and sufficient, improving PR1887's ten-transfer construction by 20% in transfer count. The new word changes both the source order and boundary pairs.
- **Two-root boundary:** with exactly two calls per source and output, two roots cannot cover every nonzero mask for `n >= 6`, even with unrestricted invertible F2 root-frame changes and per-occurrence port choices.

An attaining family for every `n >= 4` uses `n-3` dirty roots, `2n` source-map calls, `2(2^n-1)` output-map calls and `8(2^(n-4)-1)` paid full-row XORs. It attains the source and output minima simultaneously and therefore uses the minimum three roots at n=6; root optimality for n>=7 remains open.

These claims require immutable independent sources, unobserved output targets, arbitrary compatible linear maps, and restoration of arbitrary dirty roots. Written all-n arguments and exact finite base-case exclusions have separate scopes. This is a partial recursive-interface result, with no admitted supplier, new κ, global weighted optimum or complete multiplication theorem.

The [README's complete invoice and backend comparison](https://github.com/conorholds/integer-mult-bounds/blob/040351abe1c0442acec4c985b074959420e42e51/research/scalable-dirty-connectors/README.md#exact-interface-and-invoice) charge actual child ports, transfers, added roots, preparation and control, with fixture-specific resident reductions of 4.5%/16.0% at n=6/8 against a one-root comparator with the same B count (Apple M3 Max, five-factor 28-leaf B echoes, two-support A maps; preparation/resets/validation excluded), a Θ(1) bit-RAM comparison, and no claimed caller/tape gain.

## Task and overlap

Task: `connector-alphabet-change`; [TASK.json](https://github.com/conorholds/integer-mult-bounds/blob/040351abe1c0442acec4c985b074959420e42e51/research/scalable-dirty-connectors/TASK.json) declares **changed** scope, because the user requested a scalable extension with more roots rather than another tiny operation-alphabet experiment. The bottleneck connection is replacing repeated complete readouts with paid root transfers and hosting; selected-supplier adoption is unresolved.

Prepared against canonical main `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`, with priority revision 4 reread. Discovery remains pinned to `fe19567d22524eef6d3858c537aeed537ad5a7e6`; historical source pins are preserved, including older guidance, and the scientific predecessors still match current main. [SOURCES.json](https://github.com/conorholds/integer-mult-bounds/blob/040351abe1c0442acec4c985b074959420e42e51/research/scalable-dirty-connectors/SOURCES.json) records exact predecessor heads/blobs/hashes.

A final canonical-main and newest-100-PR delta check at 2026-10-14 20:37:16 UTC found no additional connector-related submissions since the full snapshot. Fresh overlap covered 392 open PRs, 804 discussion/comment records and 1,931 all-state PR bodies; timestamps are recorded in TASK.json. Adam Gall's concurrent [PR2065](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2065), head `2721b1e31d718a6e70266a99521f629ce2e1d259`, publishes the same six-transfer five-source endpoint as our earlier [public math package](https://github.com/conorholds/math/tree/e3a5f7b110ac37be3d96cb147c026d18579193ba/integer-mult-bounds/research/bidirectional-universal-five); that predecessor is excluded from this PR and is not claimed as new here. [PR2063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2063) addresses five-source one-root tariffs, while Aaron Wang's [PR2056](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2056) and [PR2128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2128), the latter at `697369a971eed02c0fbcd75ebefec9f59945f08e`, use combined pair-source calls excluded by this alphabet, at five and six sources respectively. Cinna Davis's [PR2134](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2134) uses a combined TRIO call and sixteen source-map applications, also outside our model. No exact overlap for the three submitted claims was found in checked records; this is not a novelty guarantee.

## Validation

From the upstream repository root, with standard-library Python 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/scalable-dirty-connectors --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/scalable-dirty-connectors
```

Fresh replay at the preparation base passed on CPython 3.12.11:

```text
PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS (not a mathematical acceptance check)
PASS_SCALABLE_DIRTY_CONNECTORS n=4..10 dense=460 rejected=704 extra_rejected=336 fixed_port=8
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/scalable-dirty-connectors outcome=completed
```

Checks include rectangular/singular-map forward/inverse cases, all original controls, additional extra-readout mutations, positive controls, two closed-word census implementations, independent subset-DP/pair-BFS readout minima and 61 exact readout-volume checks. No paired-call check is weakened for the star or fixed-port construction.

Native C++20 commands and environment are in [README.md](https://github.com/conorholds/integer-mult-bounds/blob/040351abe1c0442acec4c985b074959420e42e51/research/scalable-dirty-connectors/README.md#reproduce-and-verification-limits) and TASK.json. Source-bound prior native results are reused: the complete six-transfer fixed-port census checks 34,977,960 legal schedules with maximum coverage 31/32, and the eight-transfer positive fixture exercises the actual census engine on 105 pairings, detecting one universal schedule. The latter is not an exhaustive eight-transfer search. Native backend validation and 13 malformed-program/CLI controls passed. EXPECTED.json is a regression receipt, not independently generated evidence.

Not run: hosted CI, Lean or independent human proof review, selected-supplier cold replay, or caller/head-return tape integration. Local reviewer experiments are labelled as additional local evidence, not shipped replay coverage.

## Credit

Credit Ross Richardson/PR934 and PR943 for the generic connector and one-root boundary; Douglas Colkitt/PR1185 for the six-source census, Gray construction and extra-readout tradeoff; woklerx/PR1438 and Gareth Davidson/PR1498 for the two-root contract; Cinna Davis/Discussion1412, Hanson Sun/PR1615, Sagar Thakrar/PR1767 and @nedveder/PR1812 for the one-way endpoint and checks; Cinna Davis/PR1887 for the fixed-port bidirectional construction and shared leaf comparison; Cinna Davis/PR1675 for the distinct signed target; and Adam Gall/PR1915 for frame normalization/odd-parity controls and PR2065 for the concurrent six-transfer endpoint. The independent agent review supplied the stronger attaining comparator and corrected the performance framing.

Prepared by Conor Holdsworth with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in discovery, mathematics, implementation, checking and writing, including three OpenAI `gpt-6-luna` agents (tool name "Luna", xhigh reasoning) on separate interface, obstruction and backend questions. Anthropic Claude supplied AI-assisted independent review, the stronger extra-readout comparator, performance/attribution corrections and review memory notes; its exact model was not recorded. Agent reviews are AI-assisted checks, not independent human peer review. New work is Apache-2.0; source notices and attribution are retained.

## Open next questions

See [TASK.json](https://github.com/conorholds/integer-mult-bounds/blob/040351abe1c0442acec4c985b074959420e42e51/research/scalable-dirty-connectors/TASK.json) and [README.md](https://github.com/conorholds/integer-mult-bounds/blob/040351abe1c0442acec4c985b074959420e42e51/research/scalable-dirty-connectors/README.md#open-next-questions):

1. Pin a real recursive caller, its ports and reserved dirty roots, then evaluate the complete adoption inequality; no such caller is identified yet.
2. Try a seven-source, three-root minimum-call construction in a bounded frame domain; failure of the existing screen is not an impossibility result.
3. Emit complete access/head-return traces for that caller and layout to determine whether the resident gain survives tape costs; caller and layout are prerequisites.
